arxiv-1903-01368.title: Sequential Relational Decomposition
arxiv-1903-01368.creator: Dror Fried \rsuper a, Axel Legay \rsuper b, Joël Ouaknine \rsuper c,d, Moshe Y. Vardi \rsuper e
arxiv-1903-01368.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Dror Fried \rsuper a, Axel Legay \rsuper b, Joël Ouaknine \rsuper c,d, Moshe Y. Vardi \rsuper e. The concept of decomposition in computer science and engineering is considered a fundamental component of computational thinking and is prevalent in design of algorithms, software construction, hardware design, and more. We propose a simple and natural formalization of sequential decomposition , in which a task is decomposed into two sequential sub-tasks, with the first sub-task to be executed before the second sub-task is executed.

arxiv-2101-00931.title: Sebastian De Haro
arxiv-2101-00931.description: Abstract The Empirical Under-determination Argument Against Scientific Realism for Dual Theories Abstract This paper explores the options available to the anti-realist to defend a Quinean empirical under-determination thesis using examples of dualities. I first explicate a version of the empirical under-determination thesis that can be brought to bear on theories of contemporary physics.

arxiv-2102-12218.title: Multi-Task Temporal Convolutional Networks for Joint Recognition of Surgical Phases and Steps in Gastric Bypass Procedures
arxiv-2102-12218.creator: Sanat Ramesh, Diego Dall’Alba, Cristians Gonzalez, Tong Yu, Pietro Mascagni, Didier Mutter, Jacques Marescaux, Paolo Fiorini, Nicolas Padoy
arxiv-2102-12218.description: Abstract Purpose Automatic segmentation and classification of surgical activity is crucial for providing advanced support in computer-assisted interventions and autonomous functionalities in robot-assisted surgeries. Prior works have focused on recognizing either coarse activities, such as phases, or fine-grained activities, such as gestures. This work aims at jointly recognizing two complementary levels of granularity directly from videos, namely phases and steps.

arxiv-2109-13553.title: Electron Acceleration Using Twisted Laser Wavefronts
arxiv-2109-13553.creator: Yin Shi, David Blackman, Alexey Arefiev
arxiv-2109-13553.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yin Shi, David Blackman, Alexey Arefiev. Using plasma mirror injection we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, that a circularly polarized helical laser pulse can accelerate highly collimated dense bunches of electrons to several hundred MeV using currently available laser systems. The circular-polarized helical (Laguerre-Gaussian) beam has a unique field structure where the transverse fields have helix-like wave-fronts which tend to zero on-axis where, at focus, there are large on-axis longitudinal magnetic and electric fields.

arxiv-2110-02904.title: CCO-VOXEL: Chance Constrained Optimization over Uncertain Voxel-Grid Representation for Safe Trajectory Planning
arxiv-2110-02904.creator: Sudarshan S Harithas, Rishabh Dev Yadav, Deepak Singh, Arun Kumar Singh, K Madhava Krishna
arxiv-2110-02904.description: Abstract We present CCO-VOXEL: the very first chance-constrained optimization (CCO) algorithm that can compute trajectory plans with probabilistic safety guarantees in real-time directly on the voxel-grid representation of the world. CCO-VOXEL maps the distribution over the distance to the closest obstacle to a distribution over collision-constraint violation and computes an optimal trajectory that minimizes the violation probability.

arxiv-2112-05815.title: A multivariate CLT for ¡¡typical¿¿ weighted sums with rate of convergence of order O(1/n)
arxiv-2112-05815.creator: Sagak A. Ayvazyan, Vladimir V. Ulyanov
arxiv-2112-05815.description: Abstract The ”typical” asymptotic behavior of the weighted sums of independent random vectors in k k -dimensional space is considered. It is shown that in this case the rate of convergence in the multivariate central limit theorem is of order O ⁡ ( 1 / n ) O(1/n) . This extends the one-dimensional Klartag and Sodin (2011) result.

arxiv-2208-06023.title: Non-Standard Neutrino Self-Interactions Can Cause Neutrino Flavor Equipartition Inside the Supernova Core
arxiv-2208-06023.creator: Sajad Abbar Max-Planck-Institut für Physik (Werner-Heisenberg-Institut), Föhringer Ring 6, 80805 München, Germany
arxiv-2208-06023.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sajad Abbar Max-Planck-Institut für Physik (Werner-Heisenberg-Institut), Föhringer Ring 6, 80805 München, Germany. We show that non-standard neutrino self-interactions can lead to total flavor equipartition in a dense neutrino gas, such as those expected in core-collapse supernovae. In this first investigation of this phenomenon in the multi-angle scenario, we demonstrate that such a flavor equipartition can occur on very short scales, and therefore very deep inside the newly formed proto-neutron star, with a possible significant impact on the physics of core-collapse supernovae.

arxiv-2208-10297.title: Locate Then Ask: Interpretable Stepwise Reasoning for Multi-hop Question Answering
arxiv-2208-10297.creator: Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei, Zhihao Fan, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang
arxiv-2208-10297.description: Abstract Multi-hop reasoning requires aggregating multiple documents to answer a complex question. Existing methods usually decompose the multi-hop question into simpler single-hop questions to solve the problem for illustrating the explainable reasoning process. However, they ignore grounding on the supporting facts of each reasoning step, which tends to generate inaccurate decompositions.

arxiv-2305-20045.title: ActiveAED: A Human in the Loop Improves Annotation Error Detection
arxiv-2305-20045.creator: Leon Weber, Barbara Plank
arxiv-2305-20045.description: Abstract Manually annotated datasets are crucial for training and evaluating Natural Language Processing models. However, recent work has discovered that even widely-used benchmark datasets contain a substantial number of erroneous annotations. This problem has been addressed with Annotation Error Detection (AED) models, which can flag such errors for human re-annotation.

arxiv-2402-02218.title: Machine Intelligence in Africa: a survey
arxiv-2402-02218.creator: Allahsera Auguste Tapo, Ali Traoré, Sidy Danioko, Hamidou Tembine
arxiv-2402-02218.description: Abstract In the last 5 years, the availability of large audio datasets in African countries has opened unlimited opportunities to build machine intelligence (MI) technologies that are closer to the people and speak, learn, understand, and do businesses in local languages, including for those who cannot read and write.

arxiv-2406-13281.title: ECAFormer: Low-light Image Enhancement using Dual Cross Attention
arxiv-2406-13281.creator: Yudi Ruan, Hao Ma, Di Ma, Weikai Li, Xiao Wang
arxiv-2406-13281.description: Abstract Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to improve the perceptibility and interpretability of images captured in poorly illuminated environments. Existing LLIE methods often fail to capture the non-local self-similarity and long-range dependencies, causing the loss of complementary information between multiple modules or network layers, ultimately resulting in the loss of image details.

arxiv-2407-14263.title: Magnetotransport in a graphite cylinder under quantizing fields
arxiv-2407-14263.creator: N. Kunchur, S. Galeski, F. Menges, R. Wawrzyńczak, C. Felser, T. Meng, J. Gooth
arxiv-2407-14263.description: Abstract We analyze the transport properties of curved, three-dimensional graphite samples in strong magnetic fields. Focusing on a millimeter-scale graphite cylinder as a prototypical curved object, we perform longitudinal and Hall voltage measurements while applying quantizing magnetic fields. These measurements are investigated as a function of field strength and angles.

arxiv-2408-02371.title: X-ray Flux and Spectral Variability of the Blazar OJ 287 with Suzaku
arxiv-2408-02371.creator: Dongtao Zhou, Zhongli Zhang, Alok C. Gupta, Pankaj Kushwaha, Paul J. Wiita, Minfeng Gu, and Haiguang Xu
arxiv-2408-02371.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dongtao Zhou, Zhongli Zhang, Alok C. Gupta, Pankaj Kushwaha, Paul J. Wiita, Minfeng Gu, and Haiguang Xu. We present analyses of S uzaku XIS light curves and spectra of the BL Lac object OJ 287 with observations positioned primarily around proposed recurrent optical outbursts.

arxiv-2502-10788.title: Analyzing Privacy Dynamics within Groups using Gamified Auctions
arxiv-2502-10788.creator: Hüseyin Aydın*, Onuralp Ulusoy*, Ilaria Liccardi, Pınar Yolum
arxiv-2502-10788.description: Abstract . Online shared content, such as group pictures, often contains information about multiple users. Developing technical solutions to manage the privacy of such "co-owned" content is challenging because each co-owner may have different preferences. Recent technical approaches advocate group-decision mechanisms, including auctions, to decide as how best to resolve these differences.

pmc-10585445.creator: Kaylen J Pfisterer, Raima Lohani, Elizabeth Janes, Denise Ng, Dan Wang, Denise Bryant-Lukosius, Ricardo Rendon, Alejandro Berlin, Jacqueline Bender, Ian Brown, Andrew Feifer, Geoffrey Gotto, Shumit Saha, Joseph A Cafazzo, Quynh Pham, Taiane de Azevedo Cardoso, Jiaqian Luo, Jens Lehmann, Katell Le Du

pmc-11339096.title: Exploring the influence of silicon oxide microchips shape on cellular uptake using imaging flow cytometry
pmc-11339096.creator: Gordon Bruce, Saman Bagherpour, Marta Duch, José Antonio Plaza, Snow Stolnik, Lluïsa Pérez-García
pmc-11339096.description: Nano- and micro-carriers of therapeutic molecules offer numerous advantages for drug delivery, and the shape of these particles plays a vital role in their biodistribution and their interaction with cells. However, analysing how microparticles are taken up by cells presents methodological challenges.

pmc-11399793.title: Diminishing calcifications as a potential predictor of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma arising in association with IPMN in patients with chronic pancreatitis
pmc-11399793.creator: Mohammad Yasrab, Ryan C Rizk, Felipe Lopez-Ramirez, Taha M Ahmed, Alejandra Blanco, Ammar A Javed, Linda C Chu, Elliot K Fishman, Satomi Kawamoto
pmc-11399793.description: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is a progressive benign fibroinflammatory condition involving repeated episodes of pancreatic inflammation, which lead to fibrotic tissue replacement and subsequent pancreatic insufficiency. A lifetime risk of developing pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in patients with chronic pancreatitis is reported to be 1.5%-4%.

pmc-11438821.title: Analysis of alkaline phosphatase and γ-glutamyltransferase after radiofrequency ablation of primary liver cancer: A retrospective study
pmc-11438821.creator: Wen-Yu Huang, Sheng Zheng, Dan Zhu, Ying-Lang Zeng, Juan Yang, Xue-Li Zeng, Pei Liu, Shun-Ling Zhang, Ming Yuan, Zhi-Xia Wang

pmc-11597520.title: Kinetics of RPR Decline in Pregnant Persons Treated for Syphilis in Pregnancy and Their Infants
pmc-11597520.creator: Danielle Schwartz, Alena Tse-Chang, Joan Robinson, Jennifer Gratrix, Petra Smyczek, Michael T Hawkes, Carmelo Biondo
pmc-11597520.description: Congenital syphilis is a re-emerging infectious threat in areas of North America. The purpose of this study was to quantitatively describe the rate of decline of nontreponemal (rapid plasma reagin, RPR) titers in pregnant persons with syphilis and their infants.

pmc-12481123.title: Influence of esophageal temperature probe tip placement on core temperature measurement accuracy in cold environments: a randomized crossover trial with implications for cardiac arrest management
pmc-12481123.creator: Giulia Roveri, Tomas Dal Cappello, Alex Hofer, Franziska Breidt, Othmar Kofler, Erik Popp, Hermann Brugger, Simon Rauch
pmc-12481123.description: IntroductionAccurate core temperature (CT) measurement is critical for staging and management in accidental hypothermia, particularly in cardiac arrest, where it guides extracorporeal rewarming decisions. Esophageal temperature monitoring is considered the reference method in the prehospital setting in patients with a secured airway, provided the probe tip is positioned in the distal third of the esophagus behind the heart.

However, its effectiveness and safety in frail older adults with a recent stroke or TIA are uncertain, leading to variations in clinical practice.

pmc-12735064.title: New Universal Bulk-Fill Composites with Translucency Shift: Impact of Rapid Curing and Ageing on Polymerisation and Mechanical Properties
pmc-12735064.creator: Danijela Marovic, Matej Par, Eva Mandic, Tena Smiljanic, Visnja Negovetic Mandic, Vlatko Panduric, Zrinka Tarle, Bongju Kim
pmc-12735064.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study investigated real-time polymerisation kinetics and mechanical properties under accelerated ageing of novel universal bulk-fill composites incorporating reversible addition–fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) agent ß-allyl sulfone, designed for anterior and posterior applications. Five bulk-fill composites were tested: Tetric Plus Fill and Tetric Plus Flow (new universal composites); their predecessors, Tetric PowerFill and Tetric PowerFlow (Ivoclar); and RAFT-free Ecosite Bulk Fill (DMG). Specimens were polymerised for 3 s (~3000 mW/cm2), 10 s (~1200 mW/cm2), or 20 s (~1200 mW/cm2).

pmc-13250399.creator: Akiko Watanabe, Katherine L Gill, Kuan‐Fu Chen, Hannah M Jones, Mailys De Sousa Mendes, Iain Gardner, Masakatsu Kotsuma

pmc-13452760.title: Predictive pre-resection robotic ligament balancing in total knee arthroplasty is accurate across surgeons and patient factors
pmc-13452760.creator: Alexander D Orsi, Vasili Karas, Jeffrey DeClaire, Andrew Lehman, Christopher Plaskos, Simon Coffey, Jeffrey Lawrence
pmc-13452760.description: New robotic total knee arthroplasty (TKA) technology enables force-controlled pre-resection joint gap assessment. Its accuracy across surgeons and patient factors remains unknown. This study evaluated how accurately this technology achieved planned joint gaps and whether accuracy was influenced by surgeon, preoperative deformity, sex, BMI, and age. Six hundred seventy-two consecutive robotic TKAs from five surgeons were retrospectively reviewed.

pmc-13559605.title: Translating gut microbiome research into therapies for type 1 diabetes
pmc-13559605.creator: Shanti P. Kok, Max Nieuwdorp, Elena Rampanelli
pmc-13559605.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterised by the loss of functional pancreatic β‐cells, for which lifelong insulin therapy remains the standard of care. Given that the gut microbiome can influence host health and that shifts in gut microbial profiles have been observed in T1D, growing interest has emerged in the role of the gut microbiome in T1D, particularly for its therapeutic potential.

uslaw-usc-t16-s141c.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 1 (National Parks, Military Parks, Monuments, And Seashores); Subchapter XV (Wind Cave National Park).
